A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MonoSOWA work, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally includes supplementary Sections VI–VII, which were included in the comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original KITTI and KITTI-360 detection results, cross-dataset and semi-supervised experiments, and ablations in Tables I–VI.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds Waymo results, direct pseudo-label evaluation, component and input ablations, runtime measurements, and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The tracking, stationary/moving branches, SCC fitting, COS transformation and MonoDETR detector are retained; naming the existing motion-handling component LOMM does not itself introduce a new procedure. However, v2 substantively revises the motion classifier from a displacement-derived p-score to a thresholded mean-motion/noise ratio in Section III-B.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual training and evaluation on Waymo's distinct camera and driving domain, including nighttime qualitative examples, beyond v1's KITTI and KITTI-360 coverage. Waymo was only cited in v1. The supplement also evaluates real LiDAR inputs as an alternative to image-derived pseudo-LiDAR.

E2.justification: DEVIANT is added to the new Waymo comparison alongside MonoDETR in Table III. The KITTI-360 detection comparator set remains unchanged; new direct-label and human-mask comparisons reuse Autolabels and VSRD. WeakMono3D and the newly discussed unsupervised methods are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The frame-count and steepness ablations change from detector evaluation on KITTI validation data to direct pseudo-label evaluation on KITTI training data. KITTI fine-tuning now describes pre-training on KITTI-360 alone instead of KITTI+KITTI-360, despite retaining the scores. The canonical focal length changes from 500 to 750, and the motion decision threshold is revised. New protocols include Waymo Level-2 distance-stratified evaluation, limited-label fine-tuning, and human-mask/instance-ID controls. These reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds joint LOMM/SCC component ablation, human-mask and LiDAR controls, canonical-focal-length sensitivity, runtime decomposition, and explicit failure examples. The aggregation sweep expands from three to six settings, and the steepness sweep adds alpha=20 while changing what is evaluated. The original COS ablation is retained as Table VIII.

E5.justification: Supplementary Table IX newly reports runtime variation using ± terms, including 1,311 ± 291.6 ms overall, whereas v1 supplies only a point estimate. The meaning of these spreads and their sample counts are unspecified. Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-training counts, or uncertainty intervals for detection AP.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial numerical and qualitative results across Waymo, direct-label evaluation and supplementary analyses. Joint-training Easy APBEV/AP3D@0.5 changes from 62.28/53.04 in v1 Table II to 64.29/58.97 in v2 Table VI; reported labelling time changes from 5 seconds to 1,311 ms. Revised settings prevent treating these as established same-protocol gains. KITTI-360 detection AP, COS-ablation scores and KITTI fine-tuning scores are retained; v1's KITTI-only pseudo-label-training row reappears as the no-LiDAR control in Table XII.

T1.justification: v1 defines its motion statistic through squared net displacement, sequence length and estimated variation, followed by p=1−Phi(z). v2 Equation 6 instead defines z as the ratio of the norms of mean displacement and variation. This is a non-equivalent mathematical decision rule, not merely renamed notation. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The contribution emphasis shifts from proposing novel COS to proposing LOMM, while COS is recast as an adopted technique. v2 strengthens the speed claim to approximately 700-fold and adds a central claim that combining pseudo-labelled datasets achieves accuracy comparable to human-labelled single-dataset training. Annotation-free training and unseen-camera applicability remain claimed.

C2.justification: v2 replaces v1's tentative explanations for the VSRD gap with a firm amodal-mask explanation. It adds interpretations concerning annotation-cost savings, LiDAR consistency, ICP divergence on pseudo-LiDAR, possible sensor fusion, and a trash-bin false positive; the distant-object limitation remains. Its claim of outperforming VSRD in every metric with matched inputs overstates Table X: Easy AP3D@0.3 is 49.03 versus VSRD's 50.86.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies the selected cameras, CPU/GPU hardware, runtime by stage, template point-cloud construction, and the viewing-angle condition for dimension fallback. It revises implementation defaults but drops v1's explicit ensemble-outlier-filter and close-frame-selection descriptions; their omission does not establish removal from the implementation. Both versions still promise a future code/model release.

R1.justification: v2 adds WeakMono3D, Omni3D and a substantial unsupervised-LiDAR discussion covering methods such as MODEST, DRIFT, SeMoLi and LISO. COS is now attributed to prior approaches, and handling moving as well as stationary vehicles becomes a central distinction from previous work. CamConv, DeepSDF, Mask R-CNN and several outlier-filter references disappear.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and contribution list are substantially rewritten. Section III is reorganized into pseudo-LiDAR aggregation, LOMM, step-wise autolabelling and COS; related work gains separate supervision/modality categories. Results are reordered, explanations are expanded, and two existing ablation topics move into a newly organized supplement.

P2.justification: v1's focal-length ambiguity illustration is removed, while its COS diagram is retained as v2 Figure 5 with a revised caption. The main qualitative panel is expanded and two extensive supplementary image panels are added. New tables introduce distance bands, component controls, runtime stages and input ablations, alongside substantial relocation and restructuring of existing displays.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked direct validation of pseudo-label quality and separate motion/fitting component contributions. v2 supplies these tests in Tables II and VII, evaluates the pipeline at Waymo scale, and adds runtime and input-quality controls, substantially strengthening evidence for its central claims. Overstatements contradicted by Table X and incompletely reconciled protocol changes temper the improvement, but do not outweigh these substantial gains in empirical support and assessability.
